additional_info.subject: Quality deviation on chassis assembly - deep dive
additional_info.body:
Impact:
Only this charger is impacted so far.
Issue:
As shown in the video attached in the ticket, the charger door can be open no matter if the lock is present.
How it has been found:
This issue has been found by the customer during an on site visit. The customer confirmed that the lock cover looked more loose than normal, and when testing they found out that the charger could be open.
How it has been investigated:
the regional team confirmed that the issue is on the chassis, as the same behavior could be observed after applying a different lock to this charger.
Moreover, it is confirmed that no bent metal piece could be observed. However, there seems to be too much distance between the soldered metal piece (shown in the picture) and the lock bolt (when closed). The on-site team estimates that the protruding metal piece is misplaced by 1-2mm.
Workaround:
the regional support team applied two cable ties around the protruding metal part to compensate the gap.
Required actions:
Kindly report this defect to QM and identify feasible corrective actions together with QM. 8D report should be open.

additional_info.subject: RE: A new case manager was assigned to 0497504 CRM:00225389808
additional_info.body:
Hello colleagues,
We received the Quality Notice for this topic. A short investigation was performed to new housings here at the factory, also compared to a Gen1 housing.
We were able to replicate the incident. In one housing were the distance between the center metal piece and the lower metal piece is 37mm, we put the lock but it would have some movement were, if a screwdriver were inserted the button could be pushed;
We performed the same test in other housings were the distance was 35mm and there was no movement.
As it was mentioned previously, this 1-2mm difference can be related to this incidence.
However, after further attempts on the housing with 37mm distance, we were able to place the lock where it was not possible to move. A slight downward force had to be done for the lock properly sit on the housing, after hearing a
click
sound.
Please check the video attached.
Could you kindly confirm if this is possible on the housing on the field?
Thank you very much.
With best regards,
David Correia
